    {
      "startEvent": 1887,
      "endEvent": 1910,
      "contextStartEvent": 1871,
      "contextEndEvent": 2011,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "only an omniscient or near omniscient mind could make the Judgment call",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Historical interdependence supplies an ordinary reason for uncertainty, rather than replacing one. Requiring near omniscience could nevertheless block any suffering-based objection without assessing its particulars (E1887–1910). Whether that protection is adopted remains unclear: B raises ethical qualifications and subsequently says he would abandon skeptical theism before ordinary moral judgment (E1983–2011)."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2197,
      "endEvent": 2228,
      "contextStartEvent": 2185,
      "contextEndEvent": 2245,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "when evidence is inscrutable on some hypothesis even if it's high given another one the evidence can't adjudicate between them",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "The proposed rule explicitly removes religious confusion's discriminatory force despite its admitted likelihood under naturalism (E2185–2228). Complexity and free-choice constraints supply reasons, so this is a protected non-slogan argument; the unresolved bridge is from unknown likelihood to evidential neutrality. B explicitly doubts whether this proposed defense works and identifies its additional assumption (E2215–2228)."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2320,
      "endEvent": 2334,
      "contextStartEvent": 2246,
      "contextEndEvent": 2425,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "we don't know nearly enough to make the claim that there is a better set of circumstances",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "After A's reply, B renews the complexity defense: inaccessible consequences and free-choice facts allegedly prevent identifying any better world (E2314–2334). This could immunize observed evils, but the passage also presents a contestable argument on defenders' behalf, says it may be wrong, and requests substantive criticism (E2334–2339). Blanket protective use therefore remains uncertain."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 2409,
      "endEvent": 2416,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "I'm not saying this General observation trumps that",
      "explanation": "A expressly limits his criticism of inconsistent appeals to cognitive limitations. After providing cosmological and fine-tuning examples, he allows that their merits may differ and requires examining the particulars; his earlier characterization as excuses does not replace that examination."
    },

      "quote": "there is some impact that peer disagreement ought to have on one's confidence in theism",
